concepts.title: Fashion Terminology: Fashion, Style, Fad, Classic

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fashion Terminology: Fashion, Style, Fad, Classic' refers to.
questions.a: Fashion names the styles most popular at a given moment; a style is any distinct look that survives even after leaving fashion; fads burn out within a season for want of design strength; classics such as blazers and polo shirts stay accepted for years through sheer simplicity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fashion Terminology: Fashion, Style, Fad, Classic'.
questions.a: A style never dies, it only steps out of fashion; simplicity is what keeps a classic from dating.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Fashion Terminology: Fashion, Style, Fad, Classic', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: life span ladder -- fad to fashion to classic

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Historic Growth of Fashion' refers to.
questions.a: Fashion as change is young: styles froze for a century until the Renaissance, Paris rose through the royal court and the silk trade with couture dressmaking, the Industrial Revolution and the sewing machine democratised clothing, Levi Strauss turned tent cloth into work denims, the 1880s gave women separates, ready to wear arrived in 1920 and Yves Saint Laurent launched the first full pret a porter line in the 1960s.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Historic Growth of Fashion'.
questions.a: The sewing machine turned a handcraft into an industry and opened fashion to the middle class.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Historic Growth of Fashion', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: timeline -- court couture to machine made to ready to wear

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Stages of the Fashion Cycle' refers to.
questions.a: A style travels a bell shaped curve of acceptance measured in sales: designers introduce it, popularity rises, it peaks with mass copies at many price levels, declines onto sale racks as copies saturate taste, and ends in rejection when buyers move to the next new look.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Stages of the Fashion Cycle'.
questions.a: Heavy copying is the very thing that tires fashion leaders and pushes the curve downward.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Stages of the Fashion Cycle', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: cycle stages -- introduction plus rise plus peak plus decline plus rejection

concepts.title: Fashion Merchandising and the Six Rights

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fashion Merchandising and the Six Rights' refers to.
questions.a: Fashion merchandising is the planning that puts the wanted goods in the wanted place at the wanted time, in the wanted quantity, at a price that pays the store yet meets competition, backed by promotion worth its cost -- the recipe for maximum profit.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fashion Merchandising and the Six Rights'.
questions.a: The merchandiser converts inspiration into design and steers planning, production, promotion and distribution toward consumer demand.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Fashion Merchandising and the Six Rights', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: merchandising = right merchandise plus place plus time plus quantity plus price plus promotion

concepts.title: Roles of the Merchandiser: Make, Buy, Promote, Sell

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Roles of the Merchandiser: Make, Buy, Promote, Sell' refers to.
questions.a: In manufacturing the merchandiser advises on fabrics and finds the best production route for the price and target market; in buying, trend analysis sharpens ordering; in promotion, fashion shows and visual skill court bulk buyers; in selling, display suggestions and market reading close the loop with stores.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Roles of the Merchandiser: Make, Buy, Promote, Sell'.
questions.a: Historical and socio-cultural knowledge of fabrics is what lets a merchandiser turn a designer's vision into a salable product.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Roles of the Merchandiser: Make, Buy, Promote, Sell', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: role chain -- manufacture plus buy plus promote plus sell

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Levels of Merchandising' refers to.
questions.a: Merchandising operates at three levels: inside retail organisations where internal planning stocks the sales floor profitably, through buying agencies that procure, negotiate, and police quality for clients, and inside export houses where buyer merchandisers link client to factory while production merchandisers keep output on schedule.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Levels of Merchandising'.
questions.a: Buying agencies save exporters cost and time; in export houses the buyer side sources and samples while the production side delivers on time.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Levels of Merchandising', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: levels -- retail organisation plus buying agency plus export house

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Target Market and Market Segmentation' refers to.
questions.a: A target market is the consumer category likeliest to buy the offering, found by segmenting the whole market into subsets that share needs -- by demography such as age, sex, income, by geography and climate, by psychographic lifestyle, or by behavioural opinion and usage of products.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Target Market and Market Segmentation'.
questions.a: Segmentation concentrates sales effort where returns are highest and reads the motivations behind buying.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Target Market and Market Segmentation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: segmentation bases -- demographic plus geographic plus psychographic plus behavioural

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fashion Retail Organisations' refers to.
questions.a: Retail formats run from the owner run neighbourhood single unit store through department stores with separate sections to chain stores sharing one brand and central management; inside large stores the work splits into merchandising, sales promotion, finance and control, operations, and personnel or branch divisions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fashion Retail Organisations'.
questions.a: Organisational structure shifts with merchandise type, firm size and target customer.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Fashion Retail Organisations', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: formats -- single unit plus department plus chain; divisions -- merchandise plus promotion plus finance plus operations plus personnel

concepts.title: Skills, Courses and Careers in Fashion

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Skills, Courses and Careers in Fashion' refers to.
questions.a: Success needs three divergent abilities -- forecasting trends ahead of time, analysing the dollars and sense of styles against company and consumer budgets, and communicating well enough to negotiate, sell and write copy; training runs from six month certificates through two year master's to four year bachelor's programmes, leading to work as visual merchandise designer, fashion designer, set designer or interior designer.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Skills, Courses and Careers in Fashion'.
questions.a: About one third of professional fashion designers are self employed, and most aspirants specialise in one area such as apparel, displays or theatre sets.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Skills, Courses and Careers in Fashion', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: skill triad -- forecasting plus analytical plus communication

questions.q: Find the paper height of a croquis from its head count and head size. Use the method 'Croquis Height Arithmetic'. Work with: head_count = 360, head_size = 8192. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of figure_height.
questions.a: 2949120 units

questions.q: Calculate the drawn height when the head unit and the number of heads are stated. Use the method 'Croquis Height Arithmetic'. Work with: head_count = 75, head_size = 8192. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of figure_height.
questions.a: 614400 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Croquis Height Arithmetic' refers to.
questions.a: A fashion croquis is drawn in head units, so the height of the sketch on paper is the number of heads multiplied by the chosen head length in inches.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Croquis Height Arithmetic'.
questions.a: Fashion figures run eight and a half to ten heads tall, with the centre front line divided into that many equal parts.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Croquis Height Arithmetic', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: figure_height = head_count * head_size

questions.q: Find the gap in years between two study routes when both durations are stated. Use the method 'Study Programme Duration Gaps'. Work with: long_years = 50, short_years = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of duration_gap.
questions.a: 0 times

questions.q: How much longer is a 4 year bachelor's than a 2 year master's in this field? Use the method 'Study Programme Duration Gaps'. Work with: long_years = 200, short_years = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of duration_gap.
questions.a: 100 times

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Study Programme Duration Gaps' refers to.
questions.a: Fashion education routes differ in length -- certificates and diplomas finish in six months to a year, master's degrees take two years and bachelor's four -- so the extra years one route demands over another is simply the longer duration minus the shorter.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Study Programme Duration Gaps'.
questions.a: Choosing a bachelor's over a one year diploma means investing three extra years for broader promotion chances.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Study Programme Duration Gaps', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: duration_gap = long_years - short_years

questions.q: Calculate the self employed designers when the total and the independent fraction are given. Use the method 'Self-Employment Share of Designers'. Work with: self_share = 0.35, total_designers = 360. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of self_employed.
questions.a: 126 units

questions.q: How many of 600 designers would be self employed at a one third rate? Use the method 'Self-Employment Share of Designers'. Work with: self_share = 0.5, total_designers = 40. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of self_employed.
questions.a: 20 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Self-Employment Share of Designers' refers to.
questions.a: When a stated fraction of a designer population works for itself, applying that fraction to the total gives the number of independent professionals -- about one third in fashion design.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Self-Employment Share of Designers'.
questions.a: Roughly one in three professional fashion designers runs an independent practice, which fuels the field's entrepreneurial appeal.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Self-Employment Share of Designers', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: self_employed = total_designers * self_share
